# Film data: provenance and licence audit

Scope: everything under `core/data/film/` and every data section of `core/data/film/dapple.dfp`, plus the numeric tables
compiled into the engine (`core/src/film_tables.inc`). This is an engineering audit, not legal advice. Items marked
"verify" were not checked against the original publisher's terms in this session (no network lookup was done).

## 1. Result in one paragraph

* The spectral-upsampling table (pack section `UPSM`) is **already Dapple's own**: it is generated by
  `core/src/film_upsample.cpp` (Jakob & Hanika 2019 sigmoid-of-quadratic spectra, minimum-norm fit per chromaticity node,
  CIE 1931 2-degree observer, triangle-coordinate (tc) mapping of spec 2.5). No data of hanatos' coefficient LUT
  (`hanatos_irradiance_xy_coeffs_250304.lut`) or of `irradiance_xy_tc.npy` is read, shipped or used anywhere in the repository
  (grep over `core/ cli/ tests/ docs/`: the only "hanatos" hits are the setting names `hanatos2025*` that the profile JSON
  and the spec use, and the NOTICE text saying the files were not used). Verified with the new command
  `dapple film-upsm-gen --verify core/data/film/dapple.dfp`: the table inside the checked-in pack is **bit-identical** to a fresh
  regeneration (FNV-1a64 of the float32 data `282b933bbed17fb2`, 192 x 192 x 4 floats = a0, a1, a2, 1/sum(s*(xbar+ybar+zbar))).
  The pack rebuilt from the profiles is byte-identical to the checked-in `dapple.dfp` (1 235 385 bytes).
* Note the stored form differs from the spec's 192 x 192 x 81 fp16 spectra: the pack stores the 3 sigmoid coefficients plus a
  normalisation per node and the engine evaluates the 81 samples itself. The tc mapping, the 380..780 nm / 5 nm domain and the
  "emission spectrum, unit X+Y+Z" semantics are those of the spec, so it is a drop-in table (the engine only ever used this table).
* rgb2spec (Wenzel Jakob, BSD-3-Clause) was **not** consulted or copied, so no rgb2spec licence text is required; the method is
  credited to the paper in `NOTICE.md`. If rgb2spec code is ever ported, add its BSD-3-Clause text to `NOTICE.md` first.
* Remaining legal exposure is elsewhere: ShareAlike scope of the CC BY-SA profile data, and the provenance of the
  Incandescent (`T`), Kinoton 75P (`K75P`), KG3 and lens spectra (section 3).

## 2. Upsampling table: reproduction and accuracy

Reproduce: `dapple film-upsm-gen [--n 192] [--out table.bin] [--verify core/data/film/dapple.dfp]` (about 4 s, single thread,
deterministic, prints the hash). Pack build: `dapple film-pack core/data/film/profiles core/data/film/dapple.dfp`.

Chromaticity accuracy of the table (spectrum -> xy through the CIE observer vs the node's target xy):

| nodes | count | mean error | max error | nodes with error > 1e-4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| inside the spectral locus | 24 313 | 1.2e-3 | 0.156 | 1 851 (close to the locus, MacAdam limit of 3-coefficient spectra) |
| outside the locus (no physical spectrum; the input gamut compression clamps there) | 12 551 | - | - | - |

### dE2000 measurements (36 renders: 9 stock/paper combos x 4 inputs, `--no-spatial`, auto-exposure off)

Metric as in `build/film/round1.py` (skimage CIEDE2000 on clamped sRGB-decoded values), script of this run:
renders in `build/film/compare/upsm/{old,new}/`. "old" = `build/film/dapple_old.dfp` (copy of the pack as found),
"new" = `core/data/film/dapple.dfp` after regeneration.

(a) our render new pack vs old pack: **mean 0.0000, p95 0.0000, max 0.0000 for every combo** (the packs are byte-identical,
so this is a consistency check, not an independent accuracy measure). Target mean <= 0.5 / p95 <= 1.5: met trivially.

(b) our render vs the Python reference output stored in `build/film/ref` (Python not re-run; the reference uses the hanatos table):

| combo | mean | p95 | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| portra400_endura_0ev | 0.0858 | 0.1791 | 1.556 |
| portra400_endura_p1ev | 0.0870 | 0.1807 | 1.724 |
| portra400_endura_m1ev | 0.0884 | 0.1766 | 1.841 |
| ektar100_endura | 0.0801 | 0.1820 | 2.026 |
| gold200_supra | 0.0881 | 0.1866 | 5.631 |
| pro400h_crystal | 0.0920 | 0.2008 | 4.380 |
| vision3_250d_2383 | 0.1163 | 0.2516 | 2.067 |
| velvia100_slide | 0.1116 | 0.2350 | 3.840 |
| portra400_scan | 0.0343 | 0.0554 | 3.053 |
| **all 36 renders** | **0.0871** | **0.2043** | 5.631 |

Both within the targets (mean <= 0.5, p95 <= 1.5). It reproduces the round-1 report (0.087 / 0.204). The profile JSONs also carry
`hanatos2025_adaptation_window/surface_params` (fitted by the spektrafilm author against that table); with our table the
residual is below the targets, so no re-fit was needed.

Not verified: images other than the four test inputs (very saturated out-of-locus colours are where tables can differ most;
max dE 5.6 occurs in gold200_supra), the Python code was not re-run, Android/GPU outputs were not re-measured.

## 3. Audit: what ships and may a closed-source commercial app ship it

| Item | Where | Provenance | Licence | Closed-source commercial shipping |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Film / paper profiles (28 stocks: log sensitivities, dye densities, density curves, grain / halation / adaptation params) | `profiles/*.json`, pack `STCK` x 28 | spektrafilm by Andrea Volpato (itself digitised from manufacturer datasheets and measurements) | **CC BY-SA 4.0** (`SPEKTRAFILM_LICENSE.txt`, metadata strings in each profile) | **Yes, with conditions**: commercial use is allowed; need attribution (About screen), licence link, change notice (`CHANGELOG.txt`), and the pack (an adaptation) stays CC BY-SA 4.0 and must be redistributable without technical restrictions (DRM / store terms that restrict the licensed rights conflict with CC BY-SA 4.0 - check per store). Keep the pack a separate, user-extractable asset. Whether the app code stays outside ShareAlike is the open legal question (NOTICE.md); get counsel before release. Author's non-binding requests apply. |
| Binary pack container `dapple.dfp` | `dapple.dfp` | Format conversion of the profiles + Dapple tables | CC BY-SA 4.0 for the profile content; Dapple-owned format | As above. |
| ATTR (attribution string) | pack | Dapple text | Dapple | Yes |
| UPSM spectral upsampling table | pack | Generated by Dapple (`film_upsample.cpp`, Jakob & Hanika 2019 method, CIE 1931 observer); no third-party LUT data | Dapple-owned (the method is published; the CIE observer values are standard data, see below) | **Yes** |
| CMAX CAM16-UCS chroma limit (64 x 720) | pack | Generated by Dapple (`buildCmaxTable`) from the published CAM16-UCS formulas (Li et al. 2017, CIE 248:2022) and sRGB | Dapple-owned | **Yes** |
| CIE 1931 2-degree colour matching functions (xbar, ybar, zbar, 5 nm) | `film_tables.inc` | CIE standard observer, transcribed from colour-science's embedded tables via the spec | Standard colorimetric data (physical measurements, widely reproduced); verify the CIE data-distribution terms when recording the source | Yes in practice; **verify** CIE terms and record the source (see recommendation 3) |
| CIE D50 / D55 / D65 illuminants (5 nm, mean-normalised) | `film_tables.inc` | CIE standard illuminants (D series, interpolated to 5 nm by colour-science) | Same as above | Yes in practice; **verify**; could be regenerated from the CIE S0/S1/S2 basis + CCT formula |
| "Incandescent" `T` lamp SPD (reference illuminant of Vision3 200T / 500T) | `film_color.cpp` `cieIlluminantA()` | **Replaced 2026-11-12**: CIE standard illuminant A computed from its analytic definition (CIE 15:2004 eq. 3.1 = ISO/CIE 11664-2: Planck radiator, T = 2848 K with c2 = 1.4350e-2 m K, i.e. 2856 K with today's c2; relative SPD 100 at 560 nm, then mean-normalised like every illuminant). The colour-science table is deleted from `film_tables.inc` | Public analytic standard formula, no data copied | **Yes**. xy of the 5 nm / 380..780 nm sampling 0.4476, 0.4075 (CIE A: 0.44757, 0.40745; `film.colorimetry` test, tolerance 2e-4). Changes Vision3 200T / 500T slightly vs the Python reference (section 5) |
| Kinoton 75P projector lamp SPD (`K75P`, viewing illuminant of Kodak 2383 / 2393) | `film_tables.inc` | colour-science library sample, source unclear | **Unclear** | **Flag**. xy 0.3152,0.3329, close to D65 (0.3127,0.3290). Candidate replacement: a D-series / blackbody (xenon) approximation; 2 stocks only |
| Schott KG3 transmittance (`KG3`) and `TH-KG3` (= Planck 3400 K x KG3, verified to 5e-6) | `film_tables.inc` | Digitised vendor curve, digitisation provenance undocumented (spec s11.2) | **Unclear** (manufacturer datasheet data, digitised by a third party). Re-source attempted 2026-11-12, not done: see section 5 | **Flag, curve kept**. Drives the enlarger source of all 8 paper / print stocks. Replace by an own digitisation of the public Schott datasheet or a fitted analytic curve; neutral filtration (`solveNeutral`) re-solves automatically |
| `LENS` transmittance, `TH-KG3-L` | `film_tables.inc` | Same family, unclear | **Unclear** | **Flag**; used only when a profile / param selects `TH-KG3-L` (no shipped profile does) - can simply be removed |
| Neutral print filter database | not shipped | - | - | Not used (own solver) |
| Dichroic colour-head filters | code | Analytic erf model | Dapple (from spec) | Yes |

| Default parameter values (grain, halation, print / scan defaults) and the algorithms | `film_params.cpp`, `film_*.cpp` | Implemented from the functional spec in `docs/film/spec` (itself written from analysis of the GPL reference) | Dapple code; the spec route is a clean-room process | Yes if the clean-room procedure holds; **recommend a legal review of the spec-writing process** since the reference code is GPL |

## 4. Recommendations

1. Ship now: UPSM, CMAX, code, the CC BY-SA profile pack with attribution (conditions above).
2. Before a commercial release replace or clear `T`, `K75P`, `KG3`/`TH-KG3` (and drop `LENS`): these are the only embedded data of
   unclear provenance. KG3 is the one that matters (all paper stocks); T and K75P affect two stocks each. They were not replaced in
   this task because each replacement changes renders versus the reference and needs a visual decision.
3. Record the CIE source and terms for the observer and D-series tables (CIE 15:2004 / ISO/CIE 11664) in `NOTICE.md` after checking
   the CIE's current data-licence statement; this was not verified here.
4. Keep `film-upsm-gen --verify` in the release checklist so the pack can be shown to contain only the generated table.

## 5. Illuminant replacement, 2026-11-12 (owner decision)

### 5.1 `T` -> CIE illuminant A (done)

`illuminant("T")` now evaluates the CIE standard illuminant A formula (see the table row in section 3); no measured data is involved.
The 81-sample colour-science table `kTab_T` is removed from `core/src/film_tables.inc`. Affected stocks: `kodak_vision3_200t`,
`kodak_vision3_500t` (reference illuminant `T`); nothing else uses `T`.

### 5.2 `TH-KG3` / `KG3` -> a public Schott source (NOT done: no source with clear terms found; curve kept)

Looked for: a transmittance curve of Schott KG3 whose publisher grants reuse. Found (looked up 2026-11-12):

* Schott product page "glass KG3" (https://www.schott.com/shop/advanced-optics/en/Matt-Filter-Plates/KG3/c/glass-KG3), which lists only
  guaranteed internal transmittance limits at 7 wavelengths (tau_i(365) >= 0.86, (500) >= 0.88, (600) >= 0.83, (700) <= 0.55,
  (800) <= 0.14, (900) <= 0.03, (1060) <= 0.001, 2 mm reference thickness): bounds, not a curve.
* Schott datasheet PDF (https://media.schott.com/api/public/content/9c99b2068750426ebaf1e459548a5bef, German; the English
  datasheet is mirrored by distributors, e.g. https://www.uqgoptics.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Schott-KG3.pdf) with the tabulated
  internal transmittance. No licence or reuse statement could be extracted from the PDF in this session (its text streams were
  not readable here) and the website's general terms were not read. A manufacturer's copyrighted datasheet without a stated licence
  is not a source "with clear public terms", so **nothing was transcribed and the current curve stays**. Owner / counsel: ask Schott
  in writing for permission to use the datasheet values, or measure a KG3 sample (own spectrophotometer data is unencumbered), or
  use a fitted analytic curve whose parameters come from the seven guaranteed limits above (facts; the fit would be Dapple's own).
  `solveNeutral` re-solves the filtration automatically.
* `LENS` / `TH-KG3-L` still exist, used by no shipped profile; remove when convenient.

### 5.3 `K75P` (unchanged; review material only)

Not replaced (owner decides after a visual check). Candidate for the review: label `D65` (CIE standard illuminant, xy 0.3127, 0.3290,
vs K75P 0.3152, 0.3329). Before / after renders (before = K75P left, after = D65 right) in `build/film/k75p/`:
`k75p_before_after.png` (Vision3 250D through 2383 / 2393 and Portra 400 through 2383, landscape + portrait rows), the individual
renders in `build/film/k75p/before/` and `build/film/k75p/after/`; "after" uses the profile copies in `build/film/k75p/prof_d65/`.
dE2000 before vs after over the 12 renders: mean 0.23 - 0.32, p95 0.69 - 0.94, max 1.27 - 1.45.

are compiled in, not packed): `dapple film-pack` output is byte-identical to `core/data/film/dapple.dfp`, `film-upsm-gen --verify`
still says IDENTICAL, and `app/assets/film/dapple.dfp` is in sync.
